title: palette.json lane_speeds loader validates element type but not range — a negative value silently freezes that lane's packets at the departure node
evidence: app/render/palette.odin:41: "lane_speeds: [3]i32, // [Express, Standard, Best-effort]" with the 3.3 canon comment above it: "Per-mille of the true along-edge fraction (1000 = full speed, 0 = frozen). Cosmetic only." palette.odin:94-104: "if arr, ok := obj["lane_speeds"].(json.Array); ok && len(arr) == 3 { ok_all := true; for i in 0..<3 { if _, okn := arr[i].(json.Integer); !okn { ok_all = false; break } }; if ok_all { for i in 0..<3 { p.lane_speeds[i] = i32(arr[i].(json.Integer)) } }" — json.Integer is i64; the i32 cast and the values themselves are never range-checked (only the element TYPE is), so a negative value (e.g. -1) passes parse. view.odin:369-376: "if int(lane) < 3 { ppm := v.palette.lane_speeds[lane]; if ppm > 0 { frac = min(1.0, frac * f32(ppm) / 1000.0) } else { frac = 0 } }" — any ppm <= 0 pins every packet of that lane at frac 0, i.e. visually frozen at the departure node, indistinguishable from a stuck queue, with no error or fallback. Values above i32 range also pass and truncate on the cast.
detail: The new palette.json boundary (3.3 lane_speeds parse) rejects non-integers but accepts out-of-documented-range integers (documented 0..1000 per-mille); a negative value silently freezes one lane's render motion. Cosmetic-only impact (render readout; the core never reads the palette), local single-player data file.
recommended_fix: In palette_load, range-check each element (0..=1000) and fall back to {1000, 850, 700} on any out-of-range value, mirroring the existing non-integer fallback.
